ratification_language: Option 2 is selected with a 300-second maximum reference age, a 120-second fill window, and no more than two gated attempts. Each attempt independently verifies quote freshness, spread, manifest-price drift, broker state, and residual-stage tolerance. Failure after the second attempt results in HALTED_REQUIRES_REVIEW; it does not trigger a market-order fallback or an automatic increase in tolerance.

single_stock.drift_reference: THE REVIEWED MANIFEST PRICE — never the latest attempt's own reference. Every attempt re-verifies drift against the manifest price, so a chase can never walk away from the reviewed plan.

attempt_policy.no_market_order_fallback: failure after the final attempt is HALTED_REQUIRES_REVIEW. There is NO automatic escalation to a market order under any circumstance.
attempt_policy.no_automatic_tolerance_increase: the residual tolerance is fixed; it is never raised automatically to make a run succeed.
attempt_policy.terminality_precondition: an attempt N+1 may not be submitted until attempt N is CONCLUSIVELY terminal at the BROKER (filled, cancel-confirmed, rejected or expired). A timeout alone is NOT sufficient to permit another submission. If terminality cannot be established the run halts.
attempt_policy.retry_quantity_rule: a re-attempt requests intended_qty minus cumulative broker-confirmed filled qty; it never re-requests already-filled quantity

transient_staleness_repoll.applies_to: quote-age and trade-age failures ONLY, and to a missing or one-sided quote

single_stock.note: UNCHANGED from v3. Observations at t=0,2,4,6,8s; horizon ~8s.

cross_asset_etf.note: v4 amendment. Poll every 2s until 30s wall-clock have elapsed since gate entry. EVERY observation must independently satisfy max_quote_age_seconds <= 10; an old quote is NEVER accepted because the horizon is longer.

transient_staleness_repoll.horizon_is_not_an_allowed_age: The deadline bounds HOW LONG the executor WAITS for a qualifying quote. It never relaxes what qualifies. A 21-second-old quote fails at t=25s exactly as it fails at t=4s.
transient_staleness_repoll.backward_compatibility: When per_instrument_class is absent (limits v3 and earlier) BOTH classes fall back to the shared top-level max_attempts/seconds_between_attempts, so v3 manifests execute with byte-identical gate behaviour.

order_policy.type: per instrument class — market/day for cross-asset ETFs, marketable limit/day for single stocks

residual_policy.unified_rule: ONE residual-exposure ledger. Aborted, rejected, expired, cancelled and unfilled-portion-of-partial quantities ALL enter the same ledger. No category of unexecuted exposure sits outside the residual accounting.
residual_policy.residual_valuation: residual notional = BROKER-CONFIRMED remaining quantity x current governed valuation at close-out — not the original expected notional
residual_policy.stage_outcome_rule: cumulative stage residual within tolerance -> stage COMPLETE with the residual disclosed as operational debt; beyond tolerance -> HALTED_REQUIRES_REVIEW

stage_limits.inter_stage: broker re-reconciliation against ACTUAL fills within $1.00 per position before the next stage arms

stop_conditions_halt_requires_review: any inter-stage reconciliation mismatch beyond tolerance

amendment_v4.frozen_semantic: For Stage-B cross-asset orders only, transient quote-freshness polling may continue until a 30-second WALL-CLOCK DEADLINE. A quote is executable only when its INSTANTANEOUS AGE is <= 10 seconds and every existing spread, drift, notional, position, identity and risk gate also passes. The 30 seconds is a WAITING HORIZON, NEVER AN ALLOWED QUOTE AGE.
amendment_v4.evidence: 2026-08-13 pre-manifest viability protocol, VIABILITY_VERDICT_20260813.json. UUP and KMLM produce good quotes less frequently, not bad quotes: half-spread median 1.78/1.74 bps and max 3.55/8.72 bps against a 25 bps cap, ZERO breaches in 240 observations; but inter-update gaps reached 18.51s (UUP) and 20.35s (KMLM) against a re-poll horizon of only ~8s. The worst-case DEAD ZONE is max_gap - 10s = 10.35s, so a 30s horizon carries roughly 3x margin.

the_defect_this_fixes.D1_unit_mismatch: Executor v7 check_stop_conditions() took its abort count from ResidualLedger.attempt_opportunities(), which counts ATTEMPT records, and compared it to 0.10 * stage_order_count, an ORDER count. With attempt_policy.max_attempts = 2 one failing order contributes 2, so '> 3 aborts' meant 'more than 1.5 failing orders' -- TWO failing orders halted any stage of any size. Measured on 2026-08-20: 2 failing orders (MS, PH) produced 4 abort records and halted a 36-order stage at 5.9% order-level failure. EBAY (seq 35) and FN (seq 36) were never attempted.
the_defect_this_fixes.D1_dry_live_divergence: Dry mode called core.gate() once per order and wrote nothing to the residual ledger, so a dry run logged 1 abort per failing order where live logged 2. Dry and live could therefore return DIFFERENT continuation decisions for IDENTICAL failing orders.
the_defect_this_fixes.D2_denominator_collapse: The >10%-of-stage rule is denominated on the current manifest's stage size. After a partial transition the re-plan shrinks the stage and the tolerance shrinks with it: A_exits went 36 -> 4 -> 5 orders, and at 5 orders the first failing order is 20% and stage-fatal.
the_defect_this_fixes.D3_small_stage_arithmetic: B_cross_asset is structurally 6 orders and 6 x 10% = 0.6 < 1, so it has always tolerated zero aborts by integer arithmetic rather than by policy.

continuation_policy.counting_unit_rule: OWNER RULING 2026-08-21: continuation counts FAILED LOGICAL ORDERS, never attempt records. Retries are execution mechanics and must not multiply the economic failure count. One order x two failed attempts = ONE failed order.
continuation_policy.dry_run_parity_rule: A dry run MUST evaluate the same logical-order continuation semantics as live execution. Dry mode records an imputed order disposition per gate-failed order (residual valued at the manifest reference) into a dry ledger and runs the same check. A dry adjudication that would continue where live would halt, or vice versa, is a defect.

HARD.rule: Immediate HALTED_REQUIRES_REVIEW regardless of economics. A hard failure never receives a residual budget and is never counted against a tolerance -- one is enough.

EXECUTABILITY.rule: The individual order is REFUSED and is never force-submitted. Whether the transition continues is decided by the per-stage continuation policy below, on the economic residual left behind.

failure_taxonomy.invariant: No failure class ever causes an order to be submitted that a gate refused. The taxonomy governs CONTINUATION only.

governance.rule: Adding a code to EXECUTABILITY requires a governed change - a new limits version and an ADR-compatible amendment - never a silent edit. An EXECUTABILITY code is BUDGET-ELIGIBLE: it lets a transition continue on the economics of what it left behind. Widening the class one code at a time is how a fail-closed taxonomy quietly becomes fail-open.
governance.enforcement: The executor holds the taxonomy as code and REFUSES any limits file whose declared HARD/EXECUTABILITY code sets differ from it. The declaration and the behaviour therefore cannot drift: changing one without the other is a refusal, not a silent reclassification.
governance.unknown_codes: An abort code in neither set classifies as HARD. A failure nobody has adjudicated is never budget-eligible.

residual_budget.R_PCT_ruling: OWNER RULING 2026-08-21: R_PCT = 0 for Protocol v2.x unless changed by a later owner ruling AND a new limits version. Do not invent a percentage threshold without evidence. A later calibration may introduce one.
R_ABS_anchors: ~2x the ~$127 modelled worst-stage residual at K=2 (v13_reattempt_simulation)
exactly 5.0% of account 7's $5,000 max_daily_loss risk limit
residual_budget.not_fitted: Both anchors predate the 2026-08-20 incident. The value is NOT read off the $257.27 or $757.28 residuals it now governs.
residual_budget.dual_condition_note: The budget is never an allowance on its own. Continuation requires EVERY applicable condition for the stage: for A_exits that means residual exposure <= $250 AND failed logical orders <= 2. Neither overrides the other.

concentration_trigger.measure: largest single order est_notional / total stage est_notional
concentration_trigger.rule: When a JOINT-CONSTRUCTION stage's largest single order is >= the threshold, that stage is declared completeness_required = true in the manifest: ANY failed logical order halts it. A partial joint construction is a DIFFERENT allocation, not a smaller one.
concentration_trigger.ruling_v2_0: 2026-08-21 (first ruling): approve 50%. Do NOT hard-code 'Stage B is always 6/6' - let the concentration test derive it. On 2026-08-21 UUP was 65.3% of Stage B.
concentration_trigger.ruling_v2_1: 2026-08-21 (second ruling): SCOPE IT. 'Concentration-triggered completeness applies only to stages whose semantics are joint-construction completeness sensitive; for v2.0 that means B_cross_asset only. It does not apply to A_exits or C_equity.' A_exits is a de-risking stage governed by a residual-risk budget; the joint-construction justification fits Stage B, not exits.
concentration_trigger.the_pathology_this_removes: Under v2.0 the trigger was declared for all three stages, so a Stage A that collapsed to one or two residual exits became completeness-required and zero-tolerance again - the exact stage-denominator pathology Protocol v2 was built to fix. A one-order Stage A halted on a $124.47 residual, half the budget, merely because that order is mathematically 100% of its own stage.
intended_behaviour_after_the_correction: one-order Stage A, $124 residual: the stale-reference gate still REFUSES the order; the residual is recorded; $124 < $250; failed logical orders 1 <= backstop 2; therefore Stage A may COMPLETE with disclosed operational debt
two failed Stage-A orders totalling > $250: HALT on the economic budget
concentration_trigger.observability_note: largest_order_share_of_stage is still computed and disclosed for EVERY stage. Only the completeness CONSEQUENCE is scoped.

stage_A_exits.rationale: Exits are de-risking and independent of one another: a refused exit leaves exactly one measurable legacy position, it does not make the remaining exits a different plan. Governed economically by the budget plus the absolute backstop. NOT joint-construction, so concentration never makes this stage completeness-required (owner ruling 2026-08-21, second ruling).

stage_B_cross_asset.rationale: An interdependent sleeve: the legs are sized against each other, so a partial sleeve is a different allocation rather than a smaller one. This is the ONLY joint-construction stage in v2.1, and therefore the only stage the concentration trigger can make completeness-required. If the sleeve ever flattens below the trigger it falls back to the budget.

stage_C_equity_entries.rationale: Many small, individually unimportant entries; no leg is sized against another, so it is not joint-construction. Backstop 3 rather than 2 keeps the 10% count rule meaningful: with 36 orders three economically small failures may continue and the fourth halts. Both thresholds apply independently and the stricter binds.

evaluation_order: 1. HARD failure           -> halt (raised at the point of failure)
2. completeness_required  -> halt if failed_logical_orders > 0 (joint-construction stages only)
3. residual budget        -> halt if stage_residual_usd > effective budget
4. absolute backstop      -> halt if failed_logical_orders > backstop_failed_orders
5. count rule (mode residual_budget_and_count) -> halt if failed_logical_orders > max(floor_orders, floor(pct_of_stage_orders * stage_order_count))
All applicable conditions must remain satisfied. The first binding condition names the halt; no rule is subordinate to or disabled by another.

residual_debt_rule.rule: OWNER RULING 2026-08-21: a PERMITTED residual creates a first-class operational-debt obligation. It is carried into subsequent planning and must never disappear because the symbol later re-enters the target universe.
residual_debt_rule.cleanup_rule: Re-evaluate at the next eligible trading session and incorporate explicitly into the next governed rebalance/cleanup plan. It may remain outstanding only while it continues to satisfy the residual-risk budget.
must_not: automatically block /start when the amended protocol explicitly permits that residual
residual_debt_rule.epoch_disclosure: The C40 epoch-boundary record must disclose any residual operational debt present at activation.

lifecycle.rule: An obligation leaves OPEN only into one of the terminal statuses above, and only by an appended event; the OPEN event is never rewritten.
lifecycle.target_reentry_rule: OWNER RULING 2026-08-21: a residual symbol re-entering the target universe does NOT close its obligation. Closing it that way requires the explicit terminal status RESOLVED_TARGET_REENTERED_WITH_OWNER_ACCEPTANCE and a recorded owner acceptance. Silent closure is exactly the disappearance the debt ledger exists to prevent: the position stops being a residual we owe a decision on and starts looking like a position we chose.
lifecycle.enforcement: v13_residual_debt.close() refuses any status outside the terminal set, and refuses RESOLVED_TARGET_REENTERED_WITH_OWNER_ACCEPTANCE without an owner-acceptance reference. The planner reports conflicts; it never closes.

retired_owner_override.replacement: Hard/global gates: every one must PASS. Order-level HARD failure: immediate halt. EXECUTABILITY failure: the individual order is refused and continuation is decided by this policy.
retired_owner_override.consequence: A single ~$65 stale-reference failure (the 2026-08-20 ALAB case, which burned manifest 30a53127) no longer burns a manifest when the stage remains admissible under its approved continuation policy.
retired_owner_override.why: It aligned owner authorization with the governed executor instead of layering an undocumented zero-tolerance rule above it.

historical_validity.claim: Protocol v2 does NOT rewrite history. The 2026-08-20 live halt remains valid and still halts under v2.
historical_validity.evidence: Stage A residual reached $257.27 against the pre-existing $250 budget, so the economic clause halts it on its own, independently of any count rule. Replayed as case C1 in PROTOCOL_V2_POLICY_REPLAY_20260821.json (sha 955ca9cdb82a912226ae07e59bb100145dbab9299601f3fe9ef733e7b497ad02).

precedence_rule.ruling: Owner 2026-08-21: 'Stage continuation requires ALL applicable continuation conditions to remain satisfied; the first binding condition determines the halt reason, but no rule is subordinate or disabled by another.'
precedence_rule.consequence: Where two conditions overlap, whichever is stricter binds. At a 36-order Stage C the backstop (3) and the count rule (max(2, floor(0.10 x 36)) = 3) coincide; on a smaller Stage C the count rule is stricter and binds first. Neither disables the other.
precedence_rule.disclosure_requirement: The manifest MUST disclose every applicable threshold per stage (effective_budget_usd, backstop_failed_orders and, where the mode carries it, count_rule_allowed_failed_orders) and the executor MUST report the actual binding clause.

activation_invariants.rule: No live transition may begin unless ALL of the following hold. Each is fail-closed: an invariant that cannot be evaluated is treated as failed.
invariants: the manifest's continuation_policy_resolved matches the policy re-derived from the sealed limits
the manifest's embedded limits are byte-identical in content to the sealed limits file on disk, and the sealed file is the authority the executor actually applies
dry-run and live evaluate the same logical-order continuation semantics
the residual-debt ledger is present-or-creatable, append-only and parseable
broker and platform ledger state reconcile, with no unexpected open orders and no drift from the manifest's pre_run_state
no earlier halted transition remains unresolved - every run whose stage status reached HALTED_REQUIRES_REVIEW has a sealed disposition record
activation_invariants.note: These bridge design semantics to the activation gate. They are preconditions for BEGINNING a run, not additional stage-continuation rules.
